papers.title_en: Neuromorphic Decoding and Dynamical Image Reconstruction from Populations of Spiking Retinal Ganglion Cells
papers.evidence: 从视网膜神经节细胞脉冲活动重建动态视觉刺激
papers.tldr: 本研究针对动态视觉场景解码，构建端到端脉冲神经网络直接处理视网膜神经节细胞群脉冲，同时重建图像和跟踪位置。在离体小鼠视网膜数据上，网络以5.4M参数取得高达0.93的SSIM和1.33像素跟踪误差，计算能耗比同架构人工网络低约70倍，证明脉冲域解码高效适合视觉假体。
papers.abstract_en: Decoding visual stimuli from the spiking activity of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) informs both our understanding of the retinal code and the design of visual prostheses. Natural vision is dynamic, yet state-of-the-art decoders mostly reconstruct single frames with artificial neural networks that process dense, continuous-valued signals rather than the retina's sparse, asynchronous spikes. We asked whether dynamic scenes can be reconstructed and tracked entirely within the spike domain, and at what computational cost. We built an end-to-end spiking neural network (SNN) whose neurons integrate the recorded RGC spikes over time. Populations of up to 1836 RGCs were recorded ex vivo from mouse retina on high-density microelectrode arrays while flashed images, moving bars, drifting gratings and randomly moving handwritten digits were presented. For moving digits, one shared spiking encoder fed two readouts, one reconstructing the image and one decoding the digit's position. Compute energy was estimated from counted synaptic operations. The SNN decoded what and where at once. It reconstructed the stimuli with a structural similarity (SSIM) of up to 0.93, refining the reconstruction as spikes accumulated, and tracked a randomly moving target with a mean error of 1.33 pixels on a $32\times32$ grid. Its fidelity nearly matched that of the best of 17 larger spiking and artificial decoders (5.9 million to 1.7 billion parameters, versus 5.4 million), and at a mean firing rate of 14.2% it needed an estimated $\sim$70-fold less compute energy than a dense artificial network of the same architecture. Dynamic visual scenes can thus be decoded from retinal population activity in the spike domain, with a compact network and at a compute cost compatible with implantable and wearable neural interfaces, supporting spike-native decoders for visual prostheses.

papers.title_en: Predicting Cognitive Tasks from Single-Channel EEG through Task-Semantic Alignment
papers.evidence: 使用任务语义对齐从单通道EEG预测认知任务
papers.tldr: 针对EEG数据难以合并、自监督表示无法有效解码认知状态的问题，本研究提出任务语义对齐方法，将实验指令、刺激等信息嵌入语义空间，训练单通道EEG编码器对齐信号与任务向量。在十类任务预测中，零样本准确率30.13%（机会10%），少样本最高74.99%。结果表明多任务同参与者数据集对训练EEG基础模型更有价值。
papers.abstract_en: Studies of data scaling in electroencephalography (EEG) and related noninvasive recordings suggest that simple wearable devices could eventually reveal more about cognitive states. However, publicly available EEG data are difficult to combine. Different laboratories record different tasks, participants, and devices. Task-agnostic self-supervised learning can exploit such data, but representations learned only with EEG signals have not consistently produced feature representations that are directly effective for decoding the cognitive state. We therefore aimed to incorporate task information by embedding experimental instructions, stimuli and response demands in a common semantic space, and trained an EEG encoder to align signals from a single anterior--posterior differential channel with those task vectors. This framework supports zero-shot prediction without target-condition calibration and few-shot prediction using labeled samples. On a reserved ten-class evaluation, the highest observed zero-shot balanced accuracy was 30.13% (chance 10%). In a separate developmental few-shot experiment, balanced accuracy reached 34.47% using 16 labeled EEG examples per class from another participant, and 74.99% using examples from the test participant's own task recording. Our experiments suggest that training models on datasets with multiple tasks per participant appeared useful, whereas adding datasets containing only one or a few tasks sometimes reduced established performance despite broader task coverage. These exploratory results suggest that EEG datasets that repeat varied cognitive tasks and everyday activities within the same individuals across days, devices and independent studies would be particularly useful for training an EEG foundation model for predicting cognitive states.

papers.title_en: MultiFlow: Vision-Driven Multimodal fMRI Encoding via Stimulus-Informed Source Flow Matching
papers.authors: Bui Van Hung, Hoang-Son Vo, Mai Duc Minh Huy, Dang Thanh Vu, Soo-Hyung Kim
papers.evidence: 生成式fMRI编码，将刺激与神经反应分布相联系
papers.tldr: 当前fMRI编码模型多为确定性回归，无法捕捉相同刺激下神经反应的分布。本文提出MultiFlow，一种基于条件流匹配的生成式编码框架，通过刺激信息源流匹配（SISFM）条件化源分布，利用可学习时间卷积和方差头缩短传输路径，并以DiT-X解码器融合十种多模态骨干特征。在Algonauts 2025上，单个MultiFlow模型达到0.3163 PCC，接近1000模型集成（0.3195），与20/50集成差距约0.01，同时提供不确定性估计和样本多样性。
papers.abstract_en: Current fMRI encoding models frame prediction as deterministic regression, yet identical stimuli evoke a distribution of neural responses (arising from physiological noise, hemodynamic variability, and cognitive fluctuations) that a single point estimate cannot capture. This work introduces MultiFlow, a generative fMRI encoding framework based on Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) and a formulation termed Stimulus-Informed Source Flow Matching (SISFM). SISFM generalises CFM by conditioning the source distribution on the stimulus: a learnable temporal convolution shapes the source mean with an HRF-length receptive field, while a variance head shrinks its scale, shortening the expected transport path. SISFM is instantiated with a Diffusion Transformer (DiT-X) decoder parameterising the velocity field, with sub-layer Attention Residuals, heterogeneous fusion of ten frozen vision, audio, language, and audiovisual backbones, and per-subject Yeo-network heads. On the Algonauts 2025 dataset, a single MultiFlow checkpoint recovers most of the benefit of large deterministic ensembles: it trails the 1000-model TRIBE ensemble in-distribution by 0.003 PCC (0.3163 vs. 0.3195), and the strongest in- and out-of-distribution ensembles (VIBE-20, MedARC-50) by 0.010 and 0.009 PCC, using a single trained model rather than an ensemble of 20-1000. The same checkpoint also provides stimulus-conditioned uncertainty estimates and sample-based diversity.

papers.title_en: Time Window Optimization for Motor Imagery Classification via Temporal Structure Embedded Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Huan Luo, Na Lu, Xiaopeng Wang, Ziyang Shang
papers.evidence: 针对脑机接口运动想象EEG解码的自适应时间窗口优化
papers.tldr: 针对运动想象脑机接口中固定滑动窗口与神经事件错位、现有窗口优化忽略时序依赖的问题，本文提出时间结构嵌入强化学习框架TSE-RL。该框架通过语义角色动作、有限状态机约束和Transformer历史编码器，实现事件级自适应窗口选择，即插即用，在多个数据集跨会话和跨受试者实验中一致提升解码性能，且可视化显示策略符合神经生理学原理。
papers.abstract_en: Online motor imagery-based brain-computer interfaces (MI-BCIs) typically decode continuous EEG using fixed-length sliding windows that may be misaligned with neural events. Existing window optimization methods often evaluate windows independently, overlooking temporal dependencies and potentially producing fragmented or physiologically implausible selections. We propose Temporal Structure Embedded Reinforcement Learning (TSE-RL), a framework that incorporates prior knowledge of MI event structure into a constrained Markov decision process for adaptive window optimization. First, TSE-RL assigns each window an explicit semantic role through Discard, Onset, Sustain, or Offset actions, extending binary retain/discard decisions to event-level alignment. Second, a finite-state machine masks invalid actions to enforce the temporal order of MI phases and promote physiologically plausible window sequences. Third, a Transformer-based history encoder captures dependencies across windows, improving training stability and computational efficiency compared with recurrent architectures. TSE-RL is plug-and-play and can be integrated with diverse MI classifiers. Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate consistent improvements in decoding performance in both cross-session and cross-subject settings. Visualization analyses further suggest that the learned window selection policy aligns with neurophysiological principles.

papers.title_en: Brain2Face: A Study on the Relation of EEG Signals and Spatio-temporal Head Avatars
papers.authors: Camilo Andrés Martínez Martínez, Olaf Dünkel, Kartik Teotia, Maurice Rekrut, Christian Theobalt, Marc Habermann
papers.evidence: 从EEG信号重建头部化身（面部几何和外观）
papers.tldr: 本文研究仅用脑电图（EEG）信号驱动数字头部化身，突破传统手工或图像捕捉限制。贡献了64通道EEG与高斯头部化身表情参数同步的数据集，并提出EEG到表情回归基线模型。通过自建基准验证，为理解EEG与面部变化关系奠定基础。
papers.abstract_en: Driving digital head avatars is classically done by hand-crafted artist design or by image-based facial performance capture. In this work, we ask whether spatio-temporal tracking of the humans's head geometry and appearance can be performed solely from brain signals, i.e., Electroencephalography (EEG). Since prior work mostly focused on activity and emotion recognition, this task is relatively unexplored without even having publicly available high-quality datasets and benchmarks. Thus, we contribute a dataset featuring paired EEG and human head geometry as well as appearance annotations. We synchronize 64-channel EEG with per-frame expression latent codes of a personalized Gaussian head avatar. Second, we introduce a baseline to the task of expression recovery of a head avatar from EEG signals. To this end, we propose a dedicated EEG-to-expression model that takes a temporal sequence of EEG signals as input and regresses the latent expression parameters of the 3D Gaussian head avatar. Lastly, we validate our capture and algorithmic design choices through a benchmark protocol that we introduce to this task. We believe this work paves the way towards better understanding of the relation between EEG signals and facial surface as well as appearance changes.

papers.title_en: DEFT: Disentanglement-Enhanced Fine-Tuning for EEG Foundation Models
papers.authors: Yuqiu Deng, Muyun Jiang, Zongpeng Zhang, Mingqing Xiao, Yansen Wang, Peiliang Gong, Xinliang Zhou, Yi Ding, Ziyu Jia, Cuntai Guan, Chenyu Liu
papers.evidence: 解耦微调脑电基础模型改善跨受试者域适应
papers.tldr: 针对脑电基础模型（EFM）预训练嵌入中残留的主体相关变异，本文提出即插即用的解耦增强微调适配器 DEFT。DEFT 将预训练 token 解耦为任务导向内容分支和主体一致风格分支，并仅基于内容分支进行下游预测，通过递归高斯细化、时间方差正则化、主体感知对比学习与重构实现先解耦后分类。实验在多个 EEG 数据集和四个 EFM 骨干上表明 DEFT 优于匹配的微调基线。
papers.abstract_en: EEG foundation models (EFMs) have improved EEG representation learning by transferring knowledge from large-scale multi-subject pretraining to downstream tasks. However, their pretrained embeddings often retain substantial subject-related variation, placing an additional burden on the downstream classifier, especially in cross-subject settings. To address this issue, we propose Disentangled EFM Fine-Tuning (DEFT), a plug-and-play adapter for EFM fine-tuning. DEFT encourages branch disentanglement of pretrained tokens into task-oriented content and subject-consistent style, then performs downstream prediction from the content branch. It instantiates this factorize-before-classify design with recursive Gaussian refinement, temporal-variance regularization, subject-aware contrastive learning, and reconstruction. Experiments across multiple EEG datasets and four EFM backbones show that DEFT improves matched fine-tuning baselines. Further ablations and analyses support the intended content/style branch organization.

papers.title_en: StimFlow: Synthesizing Brain Activity from Images via Stimulus-conditioned Flow Matching
papers.authors: Bui Van Hung, Dang Thanh Vu, Hoang-Son Vo, Mai Duc Minh Huy, Mai Tien Dung, Soo-Hyung Kim
papers.evidence: 刺激条件流匹配从图像合成fMRI
papers.tldr: 针对fMRI刺激响应生成，现有方法多依赖压缩潜在空间和语义特征，缺乏早期视觉皮层所需的低水平线索且需多样本平均。StimFlow在原生体素空间采用条件流匹配线性路径合成fMRI，对齐训练与推理分布，结合DINOv2结构特征与CLIP语义特征，单样本即可达到每体素Pearson相关0.371，匹配平均五样本的基线，并支持直接ROI分析和概念定位，仅需一小时扫描即可恢复过半全数据性能，利于跨被试适应。
papers.abstract_en: The inherent variability of fMRI responses across trials encourages a generative view of the stimulus-to-response mapping. Prior generative encoders often operate in compressed latent spaces and condition predominantly on semantic features, which provide limited low-level cues for early visual cortex. We propose StimFlow, which synthesizes fMRI directly in native voxel space using conditional flow matching with a linear path. This design aligns training and inference distributions, enabling competitive performance with a single sample and reducing reliance on averaging. To match the visual hierarchy, StimFlow combines structural DINOv2 features with semantic CLIP features, which prove complementary along the cortical processing stream. With a single sample, StimFlow achieves a per-voxel Pearson correlation of 0.371, matching baselines that average five draws. Generation in voxel space allows direct ROI analysis and concept localization without a decoder. Furthermore, it recovers over half of full-data performance from just one hour of scans, supporting efficient cross-subject adaptation.

papers.title_en: Siam-ALS: An Explainable Siamese Deep Learning Framework for Early ALS Detection Using EEG and Eye-Tracking Signals
papers.authors: Abdur Rahman, A. A. M. Muzahid, Istiak Ahmed, Dipto Biswas, Hua Han, Yujin Zhang, Ferdous Sohel
papers.evidence: 使用EEG解码时空神经模式用于ALS检测
papers.tldr: 针对ALS诊断挑战，提出Siam-ALS可解释Siamese深度学习框架，联合EEG与眼动信号，通过模态特定编码器和度量学习实现高精度检测，在EEGET-ALS数据集上取得0.988准确率和0.998 AUROC，跨数据集AUROC约0.98，并利用SHAP提供可解释性。
papers.abstract_en: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) diagnosis remains challenging due to heterogeneous symptoms and reliance on clinical assessment, underscoring the need for objective, data-driven approaches that leverage patient-generated physiological signals. We propose Siam-ALS, an explainable Siamese deep learning framework that jointly models synchronized electroencephalography (EEG) and eye-tracking (ET) signals. EEG captures ALS-related changes in brain activity, while ET provides information about oculomotor control, allowing the model to learn complementary patterns associated with ALS. The framework employs two modality-specific encoders: a convolutional EEG encoder that captures spatiotemporal neural patterns and an MLP-based ET encoder that models oculomotor dynamics. These modality-specific features are processed through weight-sharing Siamese branches and fused into a compact 64-dimensional joint embedding. A lightweight classifier is used to predict ALS, while pairwise metric learning helps the model learn more effective patterns from the small, diverse ALS datasets. Performance was evaluated on the public EEGET-ALS dataset using strict subject-level cross-validation, where Siam-ALS achieved an accuracy of 0.988 and an AUROC of 0.998, demonstrating strong performance compared with classical machine learning, DL, and non-Siamese fusion approaches. Cross-dataset evaluation on the independent BigP3BCI dataset achieved an AUROC of approximately 0.98, supporting the generalization capability of Siam-ALS across different BCI paradigms. To enhance interpretability, six XAI methods were evaluated in the learned embedding space, with SHAP achieving the highest, though statistically comparable, fidelity in identifying important EEG and ET patterns that contribute to ALS predictions. Overall, Siam-ALS provides an accurate, generalizable, and explainable framework for multimodal ALS detection.

papers.title_en: HyBRA-EEG: Hyperbolic Global-Local Brain-Region Aggregation for Self-Supervised EEG Representation Learning
papers.authors: Xin Liu, Feng Lu, Wei Li
papers.evidence: 自监督EEG框架，用于BCI跨数据集迁移
papers.tldr: HyBRA提出一种基于双曲全局-局部脑区聚合的自监督EEG表示学习框架，针对EEG信号噪声、个体差异和异质电极蒙太奇问题，将异质通道观测映射到固定区域令牌空间，结合电极坐标、区域先验和特征依赖双曲距离，并用通道证据注入分支保留细粒度信息。通过区域-时间Transformer掩码重建预训练，在六个基准数据集上平均平衡准确率优于现有方法，且参数效率高。
papers.abstract_en: Electroencephalography (EEG) representation learning is challenged by noisy signals, inter-subject variability, and heterogeneous electrode montages in different datasets and recording settings. Recent self-supervised EEG pretraining methods improve transferability by converting heterogeneous recordings into unified token or sequence representations, but channel-aware designs may still encode montage- or dataset-specific regularities. We propose HyBRA, a self-supervised framework based on hyperbolic global-local brain-region aggregation. HyBRA maps heterogeneous channel observations into a fixed regional token space by combining electrode coordinates, region priors, and feature-dependent hyperbolic distances. A channel-evidence injection branch preserves fine-grained discriminative cues during aggregation. The resulting tokens are processed by a Region-Time Transformer and pretrained with masked reconstruction of latent features and region-level signals. HyBRA outperforms the compared methods in average balanced accuracy on six benchmark datasets. Under a controlled six-fold evaluation on OpenBMI-MI, HyBRA matches CSBrain in balanced accuracy, improves AUROC by 1.84 percentage points and AUPRC by 5.23 percentage points, and uses 96.8\% fewer parameters. Matched comparisons on TUAB and TUEV show higher balanced accuracy for hyperbolic matching than for Euclidean distance or cosine similarity.

papers.title_en: Joint Contrastive-Adversarial Representation Learning for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation
papers.authors: Yuling Jiao, Lican Kang, Jerry Zhijian Yang, Zhou Yu, Fusheng Zhou
papers.evidence: 无监督域适应方法，适用于跨天解码
papers.tldr: 本文针对无监督领域自适应，提出联合对比-对抗表示学习（JCAR）框架：先对无标签源域和目标域样本进行对比学习与对抗对齐，学习共享表示，再冻结表示训练源监督预测器。理论给出非渐近超额风险界，表明下游样本复杂度与潜在维度相关而非环境维度。实验在Office-31、Office-Home和DomainNet上验证了迁移增益，从零学习表示时尤为突出。
papers.abstract_en: Effective unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) requires a representation that captures transferable structure from both the labeled source domain and the unlabeled target domain. We introduce Joint Contrastive-Adversarial Representation Learning (JCAR), a two-stage framework that learns a common representation from the union of unlabeled source and target samples by combining contrastive learning with adversarial domain alignment, and then freezes the representation to fit a source-supervised predictor. We establish a non-asymptotic excess-risk bound for this procedure that couples representation and domain-discriminator estimation while separating downstream prediction, with explicit neural-network approximation errors. Under the stated assumptions and common Hölder smoothness $β\geq1$, the bound identifies a sufficiently large unlabeled-sample regime in which the downstream rate is $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(m^{-β/(2β+d)})$, where $m$ counts labeled source samples and logarithmic factors are suppressed. The labeled-sample exponent is governed by the latent dimension $d$ rather than the ambient dimension $p$, which enters the pretraining cost. Experiments on Office-31, Office-Home, and DomainNet demonstrate clear transfer gains across diverse domain shifts, with particularly strong performance when representations are learned from scratch.

papers.title_en: Spectral Considerations on Unsupervised Time-domain EEG Representation Learning with Deep Networks
papers.authors: David Aquilué-Llorens, Abel Puigseslloses, Angel Blanco, Claire Braboszcz, Aureli Soria-Frisch
papers.evidence: 无监督时域脑电图表示学习，从原始信号中提取信息丰富的特征
papers.tldr: 针对脑电信号 1/f 功率衰减导致深度网络欠表征高频信息的问题，本文系统研究了三种自编码器（LSTMVAE、VAEEG、Transformer）及一个 EEG 基础模型的频谱约束。合成与实证实验表明，自编码器虽能捕获 alpha 减慢等宏观变化，但 MSE 损失的幅度驱动掩蔽效应使其对高频有系统性偏差；增大潜变量维度可缓解但牺牲紧凑性与生成稳定性。
papers.abstract_en: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a non-invasive, scalable source of quantitative biomarkers for the early diagnosis of brain disorders, and deep representation learning has become a powerful paradigm for extracting information-rich latent features from raw signals. However, neural networks tend to under-represent high-frequency information, a concern that is especially acute for EEG given its oscillatory nature and characteristic $1/f^χ$ power decay, which risks masking disease-relevant high-frequency signatures. In this study, we systematically investigate the spectral constraints of unsupervised time-domain feature extraction across three autoencoder architectures (LSTMVAE, VAEEG, Transformer) and a state-of-the-art EEG foundation model. Using synthetic experiments and empirical validation, we show that while autoencoders capture macro-scale shifts such as alpha slowing, they remain biased against higher frequencies due to a magnitude-driven masking effect induced by the Mean Squared Error loss under 1/f-decaying spectra. Increasing latent dimensionality mitigates this attenuation but sacrifices latent compactness and generative stability. We argue that, as the field advances toward large-scale foundation-level feature extractors, it is imperative to move beyond simple time-domain reconstruction and to integrate spectral-domain loss terms and gradient-balancing techniques, so that the subtle high-frequency transients critical for diagnosing complex brain disorders are preserved in the latent representation.

papers.title_en: GeoNIRS: Geometry-Aware Pretraining for Heterogeneous fNIRS Representation Learning
papers.authors: Zongsheng Li, Shengyuan Zhu, Zimo Zhang, Hanyao Li, Shengming Wang, Quanying Liu
papers.evidence: 几何感知预训练异质fNIRS数据集
papers.tldr: 针对fNIRS数据集因通道布局、信号分布等差异难以联合预训练的问题，GeoNIRS首次利用源-探测器物理几何作为共享空间参考，将变长通道集压缩为固定潜在表示，并通过双向HbO/HbR交叉重建与时间掩码进行自监督预训练。在22个数据集上预训练后，GeoNIRS在8个下游任务中取得最高平衡准确率，且对缺失通道鲁棒，验证了几何感知与跨色团重建的有效性。
papers.abstract_en: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) provides portable and spatially localized measurements of cortical hemodynamics, but differences in channel count, probe layout, signal distribution, and task type hinder joint pretraining across datasets. We introduce GeoNIRS, a geometry-aware framework that uses source-detector locations as a shared spatial reference across heterogeneous probe layouts. GeoNIRS compresses variable-size channel sets into a fixed-size latent representation and employs bidirectional HbO/HbR cross-reconstruction with contiguous temporal masking. GeoNIRS-base is pretrained on eight heterogeneous datasets, while GeoNIRS-large scales to 22 datasets. Neither downstream data nor labels are used during pretraining, enabling evaluation under a strict cross-task setting. To our knowledge, GeoNIRS is the first fNIRS framework to explicitly model physical channel geometry during joint pretraining across heterogeneous channel configurations, and the first to provide complete source code and downloadable pretrained checkpoints. We evaluate GeoNIRS on eight held-out tasks spanning clinical and auditory assessment, pain and affective processing, semantic decoding, and motor function. GeoNIRS achieves the highest task-averaged balanced accuracy among the evaluated conventional machine-learning, fNIRS-specific, general time-series, and fNIRS pretraining baselines. Compared with random initialization, pretraining improves average balanced accuracy by 4.12 percentage points under linear probing and 3.30 points under full fine-tuning, with larger benefits when labels are scarce. GeoNIRS also remains robust to missing input channels. Geometry perturbations and pretraining ablations further show that both channel geometry and cross-chromophore reconstruction contribute to the learned representations.

papers.title_en: Latent-Space Importance Weighting under Covariate Shift
papers.authors: Yuling Jiao, Lican Kang, Yang Xiang, Jerry Zhijian Yang, Fusheng Zhou
papers.evidence: 协变量偏移下的迁移学习，可用于跨天神经解码
papers.tldr: 针对协变量偏移问题，本文提出一种结合表示学习与样本重加权的迁移学习算法，在低维潜在空间而非高维原始空间中建模，估计潜在特征密度比用于下游加权预测。理论给出显式超额风险界、维度比较和方差比较，实验表明该方法有效且对初始化和域选择敏感。
papers.abstract_en: In this work, we propose a transfer learning algorithm for covariate shift, integrating sample reweighting with representation learning. A key feature of our approach is the use of a lower-dimensional latent space for modeling, in contrast to conventional methods that operate directly in the high-dimensional ambient space. Our method estimates the density ratio of learned latent features for downstream weighted prediction. We establish explicit target-domain excess-risk rates with independent data folds for strictly sufficient learned representations with regular learned-space prediction scores and density ratios. We give dimension comparisons under stated smoothness conditions and a variance comparison for true weights and a fixed predictor. General finite-sample inequalities retain representation-quality errors. Experiments on simulated and real-world datasets demonstrate gains from combining learned representations and latent weighting, and reveal sensitivity to initialization and domain choice.

papers.title_en: Towards Modality-Agnostic Seizure Classification: A Unified Deep Learning Framework for Heterogeneous EEG and Intracranial EEG Signals
papers.authors: Ramya Sundaram, Muhammad Aslam Jarwar, M Uma, Sunder Ali Khowaja, Qurat-Ul-Ain Mastoi
papers.evidence: 统一深度学习框架用于EEG和iEEG癫痫分类，解码神经活动模式
papers.tldr: 针对现有癫痫分析仅单独使用EEG或iEEG的局限，提出统一多模态信号协调框架UMSH，整合异构脑电信号，并利用cGAN数据增强处理类别不平衡，采用EEGNet-ViT网络提取局部和全局特征进行分类。实验证明该框架能实现稳健的癫痫发作分类，展现了多模态学习在癫痫监测中的潜力。
papers.abstract_en: Seizure prediction and detection, essential for clinical treatment of epilepsy, remain the crucial task of this neurological disease. EEG and iEEG are widely used to analyze epilepsy due to its capability of capturing discriminative brain activities at high time resolution. However, existing works generally analyze either EEG or iEEG seizure activity separately, where EEG analysis has been well-researched, while more and more works consider iEEG for its higher specificity at the spatial level and signal quality. Currently, most of the existing seizure prediction systems are single-modal in nature, which limits its application to a variety of clinical conditions. Therefore, a common framework to analyze seizures with both EEG and iEEG signals needs to be developed. This paper presents a new framework of multimodal seizure classification integrating the heterogeneous EEG and iEEG recordings from different subjects and sources. A specific framework, called Unified Multimodal Signal Harmonization (UMSH), is developed for harmonizing signals with varied sampling rates and recording conditions. Moreover, to handle the extremely class-imbalanced problem in the data sets, we use a Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (cGAN) based data augmentation technique to generate synthetic samples to balance the class distribution. The proposed framework uses the EEGNet-Vision Transformer (EEGNet-ViT) as the feature extraction and classification network to learn the local discriminative patterns as well as global contextual information in the multimodal seizure data. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for robust seizure classification, emphasizing the potential of integrated EEG-iEEG multimodal learning in advancing next-generation epilepsy monitoring and clinical decision-support systems.
